correctness.rationale: Stationarity lets one add a voter at either end of the contiguous middle window. Only the two endpoint-and-count events change the majority indicator. In a gain word there are m+2 ones and m+1 zeros, but with final state 1 the outgoing counts are m+1 from each state. The equal endpoints imply N01=N10, so N11=N00 as well. Complementation bijects gains and losses, preserves transition factors exactly, and changes only initial mass from pi1 to pi0, a ratio t/s. Thus the signed increment is (1-t/s) times gain mass. The gain event contains a word for every m, including 101 for m=0, and every word has positive mass. When s=t complementation gives J_m=1/2 at every size; otherwise the bounded indicators converge in expectation to the appropriate endpoint by the Markov ergodic theorem. No assumption on the sign of 1-s-t is used. The exact-rational checker was read, not run: its majority cross-check reaches 11 voters; its separate gain/loss and complement checks cover m=0 through 3 only. This finite scope does not restrict the proof.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim is the exact endpoint-pivotal identity and hence strict monotonicity for stationary serial Markov votes in contiguous odd windows. It is not a priority claim for monotonicity with independent voters or asymptotic success under dependence. Accessible comparisons do not establish equivalent coverage; the precise scope of Berend–Sapir (2007) remains unresolved.
residual_risks: The 2007 dependent-subcommittee paper could have a general criterion that specializes to a monotonicity conclusion. Its exact statements were unavailable.
A Markov-binomial identity in another parameterization or older probability literature could have been missed. The search is not a historical-priority certification.

value.rationale: Asymptotic consistency does not decide monotonicity at every finite size under dependence, and dependent-jury models can have finite optima. The exact all-size comparison for a single stationary serial law explains why neither persistent nor alternating local dependence changes the competence sign, and quantifies each increment through one positive pivotal probability.
